answer: Weight influence by bonded age: each agent locks a bond, and its voting and reward weight grows with the square root of bond times days held, like cedar rings that only thicken with time. Splitting one bond across many identities buys no extra weight, and fresh accounts start near zero, so a violet flash of new sybils can't swing anything. Withdrawing burns the age. There is no shortcut bridge: an attacker must lock real capital for months per identity before it counts, and lose it all if the ring is slashed.
